why: Each box has some pins standing on top of it or inside it. In the last row the pins get fewer: one pin on top, then one pin inside, and the series ends with a box that has no pin at all. So the book answer is option 4, the plain empty box. Options 1 and 2 only repeat the boxes already in row 3, so they do not complete it.
trick: In pin-and-box matrices, count the pins and note whether they are inside or on top of the box, row by row.
note: Drawing is faithful. The book's rule is not clear from the figure (row totals are 6, 8, ...); the explanation follows the book answer 4 (empty box).
